issues.description: Whole script file is shipped through RPC payload when a path already exists
issues.detail: The RPC already returns pipeline_package_path. Adding script_content inlines the entire compiled script into every compile response, even when no one downloads it. The data structure is wrong: the server already has a file on disk, and the frontend already knows its path. Expose a small read/download endpoint (input: path, output: bytes) and let the UI fetch on click. That is the Unix-filter shape — one tool reads, one tool serves, the compile response stays small.

issues.description: compiledContent threaded through three layers of component state for a one-shot action
issues.detail: compiledContent is added to Commands return, DeployProgressState, and DeploysProgress props, then passed into DeployProgress just so a click handler can wrap it in a Blob. That is a lot of plumbing carrying a potentially large string through React state. A fetch-on-click against a path keeps the data out of component state entirely; the click handler becomes the filter, not the storage.

issues.description: File read assumes UTF-8 and no size limit
issues.detail: open(script_path) with no encoding and no size guard will blow up on non-ASCII locales and will happily load arbitrarily large compiled scripts into memory and across the wire. If the path approach is kept anyway, at least pin encoding='utf-8' and bound the read. Better: don't read here at all.

issues.description: Download anchor built imperatively instead of declaratively
issues.detail: createElement('a'), appendChild, click, removeChild, revokeObjectURL is the classic clever-imperative pattern. A plain <a href={url} download={fileName}> rendered when content is available is shorter, obvious, and avoids DOM mutation in an event handler. Small thing, but the simpler shape is right there.

issues.description: Download icon is a bare icon with onClick, not a button
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick is not a button — no keyboard activation, no focus ring, no role. Wrap it in a button (or IconButton, consistent with the sibling <a>) so the affordance matches the data: this is an action, render it as one.

review.summary: The feature is fine; the data shape is wrong. A file already exists on disk and its path is already returned — instead of adding a download endpoint that streams that path, the patch inlines the full script content into the compile RPC response and threads it through three React layers as state. That is a lot of plumbing carrying a payload that may never be used. Replace it with a small read-by-path endpoint and a declarative <a download>; the algorithm becomes obvious and the state goes away. Secondary nits: no encoding or size bound on the server read, and the icon-with-onClick should be a real button.
